Aruba's General Audit Chamber, reviewing the country's 2001-2004 annual accounts, found that contributions paid into an earmarked account held at the Centrale Bank van Aruba in the country's name for the Fondo Desaroyo Aruba foundation were not accounted for completely, correctly and on time. Source says: Central Bank of Malta (Malta). Cabinet of Malta pressured, dismissed or prosecuted officials of the Central Bank of Malta (Malta). The Shift News reported that Edward Scicluna stepped aside from his functions as governor of the Central Bank of Malta while facing criminal charges, and that deputy governor Alexander Demarco would replace him. n:Cabinet of Solomon Islands.box:

Cabinet of Solomon Islands

Honiara, Solomon Islands

1 central bank tied to it.

OWNS SHARES OR SITS IN ITS GOVERNANCE (CENTRAL BANK OF SOLOMON ISLANDS (SOLOMON ISLANDS))
Source says: Central Bank of Solomon Islands (Solomon Islands). Cabinet of Solomon Islands appoints or directs the board of the Central Bank of Solomon Islands (Solomon Islands). Under the Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012, which the bank publishes, section 37 says the Minister for Finance may, with the approval of Cabinet, give the Central Bank written directions where the Minister is of the opinion that coordination of monetary and fiscal policies or the public interest requires it, and must publish those directions in the Gazette and lay them before Parliament. Section 41(3) says the other directors of the Board are appointed by the Minister after consultation with the Governor, and section 41(1) says the Governor is appointed by the Governor-General on Cabinet's recommendation. Under section 44 the Governor, Deputy Governor and other Board members may be removed before their term ends only on grounds of permanent incapacity or serious misconduct, and the Governor only on a tribunal's recommendation. The Central Bank of Solomon Islands (Amendment) Act 2023 does not amend sections 37, 41 or 44. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012 (Central Bank of Solomon Islands)

OWNS SHARES OR SITS IN ITS GOVERNANCE (NATIONAL RESERVE BANK OF TONGA (TONGA))
Source says: National Reserve Bank of Tonga (Tonga). Cabinet of Tonga appoints or directs the board of the National Reserve Bank of Tonga (Tonga). The National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, Chapter 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition, puts the bank's board in the government's hands and gives Cabinet the last word on policy disputes. Section 10(1) says the Minister, with the consent of Cabinet, appoints five directors and appoints the Chairman and Deputy Chairman; section 11(1) says the Governor is appointed by Cabinet on the Minister's recommendation; and section 11(3) says the Governor may be removed from office by Cabinet, on the Minister's recommendation made at the Board's request, for permanent incapacity, serious misconduct or failure to perform his duties. Section 50(1) says the Minister may, with the consent of Cabinet, issue the bank written directives, and section 50(4) says that where the Minister and the Board disagree about a policy the Board has determined, the Minister must submit the disagreement to Cabinet to determine the policy to be adopted by the bank. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, CAP. 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition (Attorney General's Office, Tonga)

Source says: Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (Cayman Islands). Cabinet of the Cayman Islands appoints or directs the board of Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (Cayman Islands). The Cayman Islands Monetary Authority Law (2020 Revision), revised as at 31 December 2019 and still the principal Act after the Monetary Authority (Amendment and Validation) Act 2024 changed only its fees and regulation-making sections, puts the Authority under the Cabinet. Section 33(1) says the Cabinet may give the Authority written general directions that appear to it necessary in the public interest, and the Authority shall act in accordance with them. Section 12(1) says the Cabinet appoints the directors, section 11(3) says it designates the chairperson and deputy chairperson, section 13(1) says it appoints the managing director, and section 14(3) says the Cabinet, in the public interest, may terminate the appointment of any director. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. Monetary Authority Law (2020 Revision) (Cayman Islands Monetary Authority)

Source says: Central Bank of the Comoros (Comoros). Commission of inquiry of the Assembly of the Union of the Comoros audited or investigated the Central Bank of the Comoros (Comoros) or its officials. The Comorian parliament's commission of inquiry into the economic citizenship programme reported in December 2017 that, according to his own collaborators, President Ikililou Dhoinine ordered that from January 2015 until the end of his term the programme's funds no longer be paid into the Banque Centrale des Comores, and that he could not explain what became of them. The commission concluded that he was therefore suspected of embezzling public money. Rapport de la Commission d'enquete parlementaire sur la loi relative a la citoyennete economique (Assemblee de l'Union des Comores)
Source says: Central Bank of the Comoros (Comoros). Commission of inquiry of the Assembly of the Union of the Comoros audited or investigated the Central Bank of the Comoros (Comoros) or its officials. The same parliamentary inquiry recorded that the economic citizenship account TR0044 held at the Banque Centrale des Comores received payments, including four cheques drawn by Comoro Gulf Holding on two commercial banks between March 2009 and April 2010, and that the central bank booked money into the account without knowing the price at which the passports were being sold. The bank's board noted in June 2014 that 6 million euros had been expected before the end of December 2013 while receipts since October 2013 came to only 2.670 million Comorian francs, which the inquiry called a shortfall of more than 2,900,000,000 Comorian francs. The account was closed on 1 September 2015. Rapport de la Commission d'enquete parlementaire sur la loi relative a la citoyennete economique (Assemblee de l'Union des Comores)

OWNS SHARES OR SITS IN ITS GOVERNANCE (CENTRAL BANK OF SYRIA (SYRIA))
Source says: Central Bank of Syria (Syria). Council of Ministers of Syria appoints or directs the board of the Central Bank of Syria (Syria). Syria's Basic Monetary Law No. 23 of 2002, issued in Damascus on 17 March 2002 by President Bashar al-Assad, places the bank and its policy-making council under the government. Article 1 says the Monetary and Credit Council works within the general economic directions of the state approved by the Council of Ministers, and sets monetary policy in line with the state's general strategy. Article 8(3) says the Council's decisions are communicated to the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade, who may suspend for up to seven days any decision he considers contrary to the interest of the state, and if the disagreement continues he must refer the matter to the Council of Ministers to decide. Article 69 says the Governor is appointed, and his service terminated, by decree; article 2 puts the Council's non-bank seats, among them assistant ministers of economy, finance, agriculture and industry and the head of the State Planning Authority, in the gift of a decree on their ministries' proposal; and article 71 says the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade names the four supervising directors who sit with the Governor on the management committee. قانون النقد الأساسي — القانون رقم 23 لعام 2002 (Central Bank of Syria)

Source says: Reserve Bank of Fiji (Fiji). Government of Fiji pressured, dismissed or prosecuted officials of the Reserve Bank of Fiji (Fiji). Central Banking reported that government officials removed Reserve Bank of Fiji governor Savenaca Narube and replaced him with deputy governor Sada Reddy, hours before the Fiji dollar was devalued by 20%. The report says the new government had come to power the previous week and was led by the army. No official reason for the removal is given; the report notes Narube had recently warned about the economy and forecast a 0.3% contraction for 2009. OWNS SHARES OR SITS IN ITS GOVERNANCE (CENTRAL BANK OF ARUBA (ARUBA))
Source says: Central Bank of Aruba (Aruba). Governor of Aruba appoints or directs the board of the Central Bank of Aruba (Aruba). Aruba's Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), as amended through AB 2014 no. 5 and published by the Centrale Bank van Aruba in Dutch and in the bank's English translation, keeps the bank under the Governor of Aruba and the Minister of Finance. Section 18 says the president and executive directors are appointed by the Governor from a shortlist of three put up by the Supervisory Board, and that the Governor may suspend or dismiss them by state decree. Section 19(3) says general guidelines for the performance of the duties of the president and executive directors can be set out in a state decree. Section 23 says the chairman of the Supervisory Board is the Government Commissioner, appointed and dismissed by the Governor, that the other supervisory directors are appointed by the Governor, and that they may be suspended or dismissed before the end of their term by the Governor. Section 27(1) says the Government Commissioner supervises the bank's activities on behalf of the Country and acts in accordance with general or specific instructions given by the Minister. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), English translation (Centrale Bank van Aruba)
